sneakers.definition: A canvas shoe with a pliable rubber sole.

canvas-shoes.definition: Lightweight shoes with uppers made mainly from strong woven canvas fabric.
canvas-shoes.exampleUsage: The canvas shoes had white rubber soles.

slip-ons.definition: Shoes without laces or fasteners that can be put on by sliding the feet into them.
slip-ons.exampleUsage: He wore simple slip-ons for the casual event.

espadrilles.definition: A sandal with a sole made of rope or rubber and a cloth upper part.

moccasins.definition: Soft leather shoes with soles sewn to the upper part.

boat-shoes.definition: Low casual shoes originally designed to provide grip on boat decks, often with non-marking rubber soles.
boat-shoes.exampleUsage: The boat shoes had textured rubber soles.

platform-shoes.definition: Shoes with very thick soles that raise the wearer's feet higher off the ground.
platform-shoes.exampleUsage: The costume display included platform shoes.

high-tops.definition: Shoes, especially sneakers, that extend upward to cover or support the ankle.
high-tops.exampleUsage: The high-tops reached above his ankles.

low-tops.definition: Shoes, especially sneakers, cut below the ankle.
low-tops.exampleUsage: She chose low-tops for everyday wear.

skate-shoes.definition: Casual shoes designed for skateboarding, often with flat grippy soles and reinforced areas.
skate-shoes.exampleUsage: The skate shoes had flat rubber soles.

oxford-shoes.definition: Formal lace-up shoes with a closed-lacing design in which the eyelet sections are sewn under the front part of the shoe.
oxford-shoes.exampleUsage: The suit was paired with polished Oxford shoes.

derby-shoes.definition: Lace-up shoes with an open-lacing design in which the eyelet sections are sewn on top of the shoe upper.
derby-shoes.exampleUsage: The Derby shoes had visible open lacing.

loafers.definition: Low shoes that slip on without laces.

brogues.definition: Sturdy shoes decorated with small punched holes.

monk-strap.definition: A shoe fastened with one or more straps and buckles instead of laces.
monk-strap.exampleUsage: The monk-strap shoe had a single metal buckle.

pumps.definition: Women's low-cut shoes, often with a heel.

stilettos.definition: A small dagger with a tapered blade.

kitten-heels.definition: Shoes with short, slender heels that are lower than typical high heels.
kitten-heels.exampleUsage: The display featured shoes with kitten heels.

block-heels.definition: Shoes with broad, solid heels that have a block-like shape.
block-heels.exampleUsage: The block heels had a wide base.

dress-shoes.definition: Shoes designed to be worn with formal or smart clothing.
dress-shoes.exampleUsage: He wore dress shoes with a suit.

ankle-boots.definition: Boots that cover the foot and reach to around the ankle.
ankle-boots.exampleUsage: The ankle boots stopped just above her ankles.

knee-high-boots.definition: Boots with shafts that reach to around the knee.
knee-high-boots.exampleUsage: The knee-high boots reached just below the knees.

combat-boots.definition: Strong lace-up boots originally associated with military use and now also worn as fashion footwear.
combat-boots.exampleUsage: The fashion display included black combat boots.

chelsea-boots.definition: Close-fitting ankle boots with elastic side panels and usually no laces.
chelsea-boots.exampleUsage: The Chelsea boots had elastic panels on both sides.

cowboy-boots.definition: High boots with pointed or rounded toes, raised heels, and decorative styling associated with western riding traditions.
cowboy-boots.exampleUsage: The cowboy boots had stitched leather patterns.

rain-boots.definition: Waterproof shoes worn in wet weather.

snow-boots.definition: Insulated, often waterproof boots designed to keep feet warm and dry in snow.
snow-boots.exampleUsage: She wore snow boots on the icy path.

hiking-boots.definition: Strong shoes designed for walking on rough ground.

work-boots.definition: Strong boots designed to protect and support the feet during physical work.
work-boots.exampleUsage: The construction worker wore approved protective work boots.

riding-boots.definition: Tall or ankle-height boots designed for horse riding.
riding-boots.exampleUsage: The rider wore riding boots with a low heel.

sandals.definition: A shoe consisting of a sole fastened by straps to the foot.

flip-flops.definition: Open sandals with a flat sole held to the foot by a Y-shaped strap between the toes.
flip-flops.exampleUsage: He wore flip-flops at the pool.

slides.definition: (geology) the descent of a large mass of earth or rocks or snow etc.

gladiator-sandals.definition: Sandals with multiple straps inspired by footwear associated with ancient Roman gladiators.
gladiator-sandals.exampleUsage: The gladiator sandals had straps around the ankle.

wedges.definition: A block of wood used to prevent the sliding or rolling of a heavy object.

platform-sandals.definition: Open shoes with thick raised soles and sandal-style straps.
platform-sandals.exampleUsage: The platform sandals had broad straps.

strappy-sandals.definition: Open shoes held on the foot by several narrow straps.
strappy-sandals.exampleUsage: The strappy sandals fastened around the ankle.

huaraches.definition: A sandal with flat heels and an upper of woven leather straps.

clogs.definition: A dance performed while wearing shoes with wooden soles.

mules.definition: Hybrid offspring of a male donkey and a female horse.

running-shoes.definition: Athletic shoes designed to support and cushion the feet during running.
running-shoes.exampleUsage: She wore running shoes for track practice.

cross-trainers.definition: Athletic shoes designed to support several different types of exercise rather than one sport only.
cross-trainers.exampleUsage: Cross-trainers are used for varied gym activities.

basketball-shoes.definition: Athletic shoes designed for basketball, with features for court grip, support, and repeated direction changes.
basketball-shoes.exampleUsage: The player laced up basketball shoes before practice.

soccer-cleats.definition: Football shoes with studs or cleats on the soles to improve grip on grass or turf.
soccer-cleats.exampleUsage: The player checked that the soccer cleats suited the playing surface.

tennis-shoes.definition: Athletic shoes designed for movement and traction on tennis courts.
tennis-shoes.exampleUsage: She wore tennis shoes with non-marking soles.

climbing-shoes.definition: Close-fitting shoes with sticky rubber soles designed for rock-climbing surfaces.
climbing-shoes.exampleUsage: The climber wore properly fitted climbing shoes at the indoor wall.

cycling-shoes.definition: Shoes designed for cycling, often with stiff soles and sometimes fittings that connect to bicycle pedals.
cycling-shoes.exampleUsage: The cycling shoes had stiff soles for pedaling.

dance-shoes.definition: Footwear designed for a particular type of dance, with soles and support suited to its movements.
dance-shoes.exampleUsage: The dancer changed into dance shoes before class.

bowling-shoes.definition: Special shoes with soles designed for controlled sliding and grip on a bowling approach.
bowling-shoes.exampleUsage: Players changed into bowling shoes before entering the lanes.
